b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's test inbox, using the 3.7 Clean node (from, subject, trimmed body).

Flow: Gmail Trigger → Edit Fields · Clean → Basic LLM Chain (chat model attached, temperature 0, maximum output length about 40 tokens) → Google Sheets · Append Row on Inbox log.

Prompt (Define below):

Summarise this email to Harvest Lane in ONE line of at most 15 words.
Start with the sender's intent: "Wants to…", "Complains that…", "Asks…", "Offers…".
Use only facts in the email. Keep order numbers (HL-0000) if present.
Output the line only: no quotes, no full stop needed.

Subject: {{ $json.subject }}
Email: {{ $json.body }}

Sheet mapping: sender {{ $('Clean').item.json.from }}, subject {{ $('Clean').item.json.subject }}, summary {{ $json.text.trim() }}, words {{ $json.text.trim().split(/\s+/).length }}.

Test email (fake)SummaryWords
Add 2 crates of tomatoes to HL-0131Wants to add 2 crates of tomatoes to order HL-013110
Rotten pepper, second timeComplains that Tuesday's pepper was rotten, for the second time10
Charged twice for HL-0127Wants ₦12,500 back after being charged twice for HL-01279
Opening hours on holidaysAsks about opening hours on public holidays7

The words column lets you prove "none longer than 15" at a glance across all ten.
mistakes: Not stating the word limit and the opening phrase in the prompt, so summaries ramble or start with "This email…".
Leaving the temperature high, so the same email gets different summaries on each run.
Sending the whole thread and signature, so summaries describe old quoted messages.
Using real customer emails as test data instead of fake ones.
b.pass: Ten Inbox log rows from ten fake test emails, each summary accurate, starting with the sender's intent, and 15 words or fewer (a words column or count proves it).
b.redo: Send it back if any summary exceeds 15 words, invents a detail, or real customer data appears.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's supplier invoices from Boss 2, pasted as email text into a pinned Manual Trigger (eight items, all fictional).

Information Extractor: Text {{ $json.body }}, Schema Type: Define using JSON Schema, chat model temperature 0:

{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "supplier":       { "type": "string", "description": "Business that issued the invoice" },
    "invoice_number": { "type": "string", "description": "Exactly as printed. Empty if absent; never invent" },
    "date":           { "type": "string", "description": "Invoice date as YYYY-MM-DD" },
    "subtotal":       { "type": "number", "description": "Amount before VAT, naira, digits only" },
    "vat":            { "type": "number", "description": "VAT amount in naira. 0 if none shown" },
    "total":          { "type": "number", "description": "Amount payable including VAT" }
  },
  "required": ["supplier", "invoice_number", "total"]
}

IF · Maths check (Boolean is true):

{{ Math.abs($json.output.subtotal + $json.output.vat - $json.output.total) < 1 }}

True → Invoices sheet. False → Fix list plus a Telegram note to Tolu: "Check {{ $json.output.invoice_number }}: totals don't add up."

#SupplierInvoiceSubtotalVATTotalIF
1Agro DepotAD-2291₦120,000₦9,000₦129,000true
2Ogbomoso FarmsOF/118₦64,000₦4,800₦68,800true
3Bodija CratesBC-07₦18,000₦0₦18,000true
4–7(four more)…………true
8Agro DepotAD-2304₦120,000₦9,000₦139,000false: caught

Why < 1: it tolerates kobo rounding but catches any real error. Invoice 8 is extracted faithfully (the model must not "fix" the total), and the IF, not the AI, decides it can't be trusted.
mistakes: Defining amounts as strings, so "₦129,000" can't be added in the IF.
Asking the model to "check the maths" instead of checking it with an IF.
Comparing with exact equality on decimals, so a correct invoice fails over a kobo.
Forgetting to mark supplier, invoice number and total as required.
s.pass: A JSON Schema with the six fields (three required), eight extracted invoices matching the source text, and the deliberately wrong invoice routed down the IF's false branch.
s.redo: Send it back if any field is wrong or invented, the schema lacks required fields, or the bad invoice passes the check.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's 20-email test set (Card 4's 12 plus 8 more, including two "polite complaint" borderline cases and a refund request with a phishing link). The figures below are illustrative; yours come from your own executions and the providers' current price pages.

ModelAccuracyCritical missesAvg tokens in / outEst. monthly cost (2,700 emails)
A: small, fast18/20 (90%)1 (complaint → spam)620 / 5lowest
B: mid-size19/20 (95%)0 (refund → complaint, still reaches Tolu)620 / 5about 3× A
C: largest20/20 (100%)0620 / 5about 15× A

Cost working: 90 emails × 30 days = 2,700 classifier calls. Monthly cost = 2,700 × (620 × input price per token + 5 × output price per token). Convert to naira at the day's rate and note the date. Put each provider's pricing-page link and the date you checked it beside the row.

Recommendation to the client (five lines):

  1. Use Model B for the Text Classifier: zero critical misses on 20 test emails.
  2. Model A was cheapest but marked a real complaint as spam, which we can't accept.
  3. Model C was perfect but costs about five times B for one extra correct label that already reached Tolu.
  4. Keep a stronger model only for drafting replies, where wording matters.
  5. Re-run the test set monthly and whenever we change descriptions or models.

Submit: the 20 expected,predicted lines for each model, the scored Card 4 screenshots, the table with sources, and the recommendation.
mistakes: Counting a refund labelled as complaint as critical (it still reaches Tolu), or missing a real email marked as spam (which is).
Guessing tokens instead of reading them from executions.
Quoting prices without a link and date, or presenting them as fixed.
Choosing the most accurate model regardless of cost, or the cheapest despite a critical miss.
g.pass: A complete table for three models on 20 emails with accuracy, critical misses, measured tokens and a sourced monthly cost, and a five-line recommendation choosing a model with zero critical misses.
g.redo: Send it back if any cell is missing or unsourced, critical misses are mis-scored, or the chosen model has one.
